context: Arm A = today's layer-level hybrid at d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 attn_every=4 (9 KDA blocks + 3 MLA blocks). confound: DEPTH IS NOT THE CONFOUND -- both arms are L12, same ffn, same d. THE REAL CONFOUND IS ATTENTION COUNT: arm B has 12 attention paths of width 256, arm A has 3 of width 1024. Total attention width is 3072 vs 3072, equal by construction, but the COUNT and the PER-LAYER width both move together and this design cannot separate them. A result favouring B does not distinguish 'attention in every layer helps' from 'more, narrower attention heads help'. Separating them needs a third arm (e.g. attn_every=1 at full width, which is +8 blocks of MLA and a different parameter budget) and is not in this A/B.

paired_corr_decision: WHAT THE PER-TOKEN CORRELATION CHANGES (added 2026-09-06 by e1, 4c's condition for spending a card on it): it decides whether block-paired scoring stays the default estimator for every arm comparison in this repo, or is retired as complexity that buys nothing. Pairing cuts the SE by 1/sqrt(2(1-corr))/sqrt(2); at corr 0.95 that is 4.5x, at corr 0.5 it is 1.4x. CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE: this row's own +/-0.003 BPB threshold was set against a 0.0021 arm-to-arm spread measured on two doccu legs, and an SE 4.5x wider than assumed would put that threshold inside the noise -- so the number that decided ARM B LOSES depends on a correlation nobody has measured. Pre-registered read, so the answer cannot be fitted to the wish: corr >= 0.90 keeps block-paired as the default and this row's verdict stands unrevisited; corr <= 0.60 retires pairing for future comparisons and this row's t=+81.12 is re-derived unpaired before it is cited again; 0.60 < corr < 0.90 keeps pairing but requires the SE to be reported both ways in any new comparison. bias_step_size: RESOLVED 2026-09-05 by reading the paper, not by guessing. gamma = 0.001 and the sequence-wise balance alpha = 1e-4 are hereby PRE-REGISTERED AS OUR VALUES, BORROWED from facts/moe.json#moe.dsv3_bias_update_speed and facts/moe.json#moe.dsv3_seq_balance_alpha (arXiv:2412.19437 sections 2.1.2 and 4.2, read at https://arxiv.org/html/2412.19437, relayed by 4c and re-read independently before landing). Both fact entries are status `recorded`, not `measured`: nothing in this repo has measured either constant. THE SCALE GAP IS REGISTERED WITH THE VALUE, because it is the reason this is a borrowing and not an inheritance: our E1 arm gives 32,768 tokens per routed expert per step against DeepSeek-V3's 1,966,080 at their steady-state batch, a factor of 60.0, and 12.0x below even their warmup batch. gamma is a step size on a control loop reading a per-expert token count whose relative noise grows as that count shrinks. The per-SEQUENCE picture is the opposite and is registered too: at seq 4096 we get 512 tokens per expert per sequence against their 128, so alpha's regime is 4x better than theirs while gamma's is 60x worse. FROZEN FOR THE RUN: neither constant is tuned after seeing a curve. If readout 4's stop rule fires, the report says the balancer failed at this scale with the paper's gamma -- it does not retune gamma and relaunch, because a tuned constant makes the arm unattributable and turns a measurement into a search. A gamma sweep, if it is ever warranted, is a separate registered row. Their gamma also has a SCHEDULE we are not copying (0.001 for 14.3T tokens then 0.0 for the last 500B, i.e. the bias freezes for the final 3.4%); our 1B-token run is entirely inside their first phase, so a constant 0.001 is the faithful reading, not a simplification. Scope, and this is the part easiest to implement wrong: the bias is added to the affinity score for top-k SELECTION ONLY. The gating value multiplied into the FFN output uses the UN-BIASED affinity score. Biasing the gate as well changes the function the arm computes, not just its routing, and the module's test must assert the un-biased gate directly.

(2) NUMERICAL TOLERANCES ARE PER-DEVICE, from tilerl's measurement (credited in facts/moe.json#moe.grouped_mm_bf16_reduction_floor): on CUDA at bf16, _grouped_mm's reduction order differs from an identical plain matmul by 0.001953 for the SAME function, while fp32-on-CUDA and plain-matmul-at-bf16 are both exactly 0.0. amendment_6: AMENDMENT 6, ruled by 4c 2026-09-05 (option a), written BEFORE the arm starts. THE ARM AND THE CONTROL DO NOT TRAIN THEIR FFN IN THE SAME PRECISION, and this is a second difference from the control on a run designed to have exactly one. MEASURED at E1's shape, not inferred: the control's dense FFN is two nn.Linear (w13 (6144,1024), w2 (1024,3072)), both 16-aligned, so train._fp8_filter returns True for both and 100% of its FFN matmuls run in fp8. The arm's routed experts are raw 3D nn.Parameters (w13 (24,1536,1024), w2 (24,1024,768)) and torchao's swap only visits nn.Linear, so _fp8_filter is NEVER CALLED for them and they train in bf16 -- 56,623,104 of 58,982,400 FFN parameters per layer, 96.00%. Only the shared expert (sh13/sh2, nn.Linear, 4.00%) is fp8. The router is fp8=False already, correctly but by accident: 24 output features is not 16-aligned, so _fp8_ok's shape test excludes it rather than any rule about routers. THIS IS NOT FIXABLE BY A FILTER: there is no nn.Linear for _fp8_filter to refuse, so the _is_mem_fqn-style path exclusion that covers the memory table has nothing to attach to here (tilerl's review item 3 asked for that exclusion; this is why it does not exist). BOTH READOUTS CARRY THE TERM, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and that is the point of registering it: readout 1's val delta carries a precision term IN THE ARM'S FAVOUR (bf16 experts are more precise than fp8 ones), while readout 5's tok/s ratio carries the same term AGAINST the arm (H20 is 296 TFLOPS dense fp8 against 148 bf16, eff.h20_specs -- a 2x peak ratio on the matmuls that are 25.3% of the control's step, eff.step_time_by_operator_complete), so a ratio near the 0.85 bar is read knowing part of it is precision and not dispatch. A stop that fires at 0.84 is therefore reported as ambiguous between the two, not as a dispatch verdict. SIZE OF THE QUALITY TERM: UNMEASURED, expected under the 0.010 nat bar. Searched facts/ (efficiency, data_scaling, base_eval, memory_layers, all 2026-09-05), docs/standards/ and runs/board.jsonl for a recorded fp8-vs-bf16 val or BPB delta: none exists. The closest entries are about something else and are NOT cited as this bound -- eff.vocab_alignment_2x_lm_head's A/B max |delta| 0.0016 is vocab padding at fixed precision, and 0830v1_gates.md's 'quality-neutral change (an fp8 recipe)' is a design statement with no number behind it. So the honest statement is that the term is unmeasured and expected small, and nothing more; a number invented here would be worse than the admission. NOT OPTION (b): excluding the control's FFN from fp8 and re-running the control costs a full control run to reproduce a comparison believed flat, which the user's standard strikes. WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: STRUCK AND SUPERSEDED BY AMENDMENT 7, see there. The struck sentence named 'a readout-1 delta between -0.010 and -0.003, i.e. inside the adopt band' and it was wrong twice over, caught by e1's review 2026-09-05. (i) By readout_1_primary's own definition that band is MEASURED-NOT-ADOPTED, not adopt: adopt is delta <= -0.010. (ii) Worse, it is the band where this confound cannot change any decision. The precision term flatters the arm, so it pushes delta MORE NEGATIVE, toward adopt -- the interval where it can flip a verdict is roughly -0.020 < delta <= -0.010, adopted as measured and possibly null in truth. The struck sentence named the interval immediately BELOW that, adjacent and non-overlapping, so a measured -0.012 (which could be -0.002 true plus a -0.010 precision term) would have been adopted without triggering the reopen. amendment_7: AMENDMENT 7, from tilerl's review of the dtype diff 2026-09-05. THREE CORRECTIONS TO AMENDMENT 6, one of them to a number I got wrong on the wrong basis. (1) THE FRACTION WAS THE WRONG QUANTITY. Amendment 6 said 96.00%, which is the PARAMETER fraction stored in bf16. The precision term does not act on stored parameters -- under --fp8 there are no fp32 masters, the whole model is bf16 on both sides (facts/efficiency.json#eff.bf16_updates_discarded), so fp8 and bf16 differ only INSIDE THE GEMM. What multiplies per token is top_k=3 routed plus 1 shared: routed active 3*3*1024*768 = 7,077,888 (75.0000%), shared active 3*1024*768 = 2,359,296 (25.0000%), total 9,437,184 -- which is this row's own active_ffn figure, recomputed and matching exactly. SO: 96.00% is what is STORED in bf16, 75.00% is what is MULTIPLIED in bf16 against the control's 100% fp8, and the second is the number a precision argument is about. Both are kept here, labelled, so the wrong one cannot be re-cited as the right one. (2) 'ALMOST CERTAINLY UNDER THE 0.010 BAR' IS STRUCK. tilerl checked independently: ten rows in facts/ touch fp8 and none is an fp8-vs-bf16 val-loss A/B at any scale. Using an unmeasured bound to size a confound is sizing a residual with a ceiling. The row registers the DIRECTION and registers the magnitude as UNMEASURED, full stop. (3) WHICH VERDICT THE CONFOUND CAN CORRUPT, which amendment 6 did not say. e4m3 carries 3 mantissa bits against bf16's 8, so the arm's experts multiply at HIGHER precision than the control's dense FFN. Readout 1 adopts on a NEGATIVE delta (arm better by >= 0.010 nat), so a confound that flatters the arm cannot manufacture a null -- IT CAN MANUFACTURE AN ADOPT. That is the verdict at risk, and it is the reason this is registered rather than noted. (b) IS PRE-COMMITTED AS THE CONTINGENCY, now, before any number is seen: if readout 1 lands at or past the adopt bar (<= -0.010 nat), the fp8-vs-bf16 term becomes load-bearing and a control with its FFN OUT of fp8 is re-run BEFORE the adopt is written. Pre-committing it is what stops it being invented after the fact. Not run now because the prereg pins readout 1 to memory_layers_0905's estimator and thresholds so the two programs are comparable, and a control whose FFN left fp8 is no longer that control -- spending a card and decoupling two programs to remove a term not yet shown to be non-zero. THE SYMMETRIC FIX DOES NOT EXIST and that is why the contingency is named in advance: the experts are raw nn.Parameters, torchao visits only nn.Linear, so the arm cannot be forced INTO fp8 to close the gap from the other side. (b) is the only lever.

But (b') has experts, so moe_diag recorded its throughput at FULL precision -- 57054.034771759914 at step 30, 56858.079626904895 at step 100 -- a sink the rule did not anticipate because no dense run reaches it. With the numerator exact and only the denominator rounded, the ratio lies in [0.8329, 0.8452] at step 30 and [0.8300, 0.8423] at step 100. THE CHOICE CANNOT FLIP THE VERDICT, and that is the whole argument: the exact-numerator interval is a SUBSET of the both-rounded interval, it lies wholly under 0.85, both point estimates are 0.838, and the loosest upper bound available on any reading is 0.8519, which still does not reach the bar. READOUT 4 IS REPORTED, NOT RULED, as pre-committed: entropy_norm 0.9878/0.9788/0.9840/0.9835 and load_gini 0.153/0.206/0.177/0.182 at steps 10/20/30/100 -- flat, with no trend, and 100 steps cannot reach readout_4_stop_expert_load's level crossing at step 500, so this neither passes nor fails that rule. The fix is one line routing tps to a sink every arm reaches; until it lands, a pre-registered ratio bar must either sit far enough from the likely value to survive +/-1.6%, or name the exact sink each side will be read from.
amendment_12: AMENDMENT 12, 2026-09-05, written BEFORE launch. THE USER REVERSED THE READOUT-5 CLOSE: speed is a cost, not the value, so E1 is NOT decided by the 16.2% structure cost. The question is what 3.9x total params (801.0M vs 206.1M) buys at 16% more time per token. E1' IS THREE ARMS, 1B tokens each, --bf16 both sides, same launch line as (a')/(b') plus its own flags, val recorded against tokens AND against wall-clock, score_matrix on every final checkpoint: (A) DENSE control, 206.1M; (B) MoE-24, the (b') config, 801.0M; (C) LATENT MoE when its code lands, experts in a projected width (down-project d=1024 to d_latent, experts d_latent -> latent-ffn -> d_latent, up-project back) at the same total-param budget class as (B). d_latent = 512, chosen because it halves both the dispatch payload and every expert matmul dimension while keeping the 2:1 ratio to expert_ffn that (B) has at 1024:768-ish, and because 512 is the largest power-of-two latent that still divides the 8 attention heads' 128-wide head_dim evenly, so no new padding appears in the projections. THE DECISION RULE, pre-registered here and not adjustable afterwards: MoE (B or C) IS ADOPTED IF ITS VAL LOSS AT EQUAL WALL-CLOCK IS BELOW THE DENSE ARM'S BY MORE THAN 0.0444 nat. That number is the standard deviation of the LARGER of the two four-seed families in facts/base_eval.json#be.one_seed_family_misstates_its_own_noise_by_2x (p02: 3.7588/3.8085/3.7433/3.7009, sd 0.0444, spread 0.1076; the other family gives sd 0.0239, and that fact's own ruling is to use the larger because understating noise ships a null as a finding). Its stated limitation is carried here rather than hidden: it is measured at 0.2B tokens on mean domain loss, so it is an UPPER BOUND on seed noise at 1B and on val loss specifically, and a rule calibrated against it is conservative -- it can miss a small real gain, it cannot manufacture one. EQUAL WALL-CLOCK MEANS: the dense arm's total training seconds to 1B tokens, read from its own log; the MoE arm's val is read at the periodic val step nearest that elapsed time, and the two bracketing val points are both reported so the interpolation is visible. A MoE arm whose val at equal wall-clock is ABOVE dense by more than 0.0444 is REJECTED on value, which is the verdict readout 5 could not deliver; between -0.0444 and +0.0444 is MEASURED, NOT ADOPTED. Readout 4's balance rule is unchanged and still applies to (B) and (C): normalised entropy below 0.70 at step 500 stops that arm. Score_matrix at the end is REPORTED, not part of the adopt rule, because no threshold for it was pre-registered here.
amendment_12_wall_clock: EQUAL WALL-CLOCK IS READ FROM ELAPSED SECONDS, NOT FROM THE tok/s PRINTS (4c, agreed 2026-09-05 after the step-200 readings). The prints cannot serve: validate() runs at train.py:3340 and tps is computed at :3357 from the same `now - t_log` window, so every val step charges the validation pass to its 10 training steps -- dense printed 68K then 37K at step 200, MoE-24 57K then 31K, and both ETAs inflated (2.0h->3.5h, 2.4h->4.3h) with nothing having slowed down. THE VALIDATION OVERHEAD STAYS IN THE CLOCK for both arms, because both pay it and it is real time: from the arms' own numbers the pass costs ~16.1s (dense) and ~19.3s (MoE-24), so over the 19 passes at --val_every 200 it is ~307s and ~366s, about 5.1 and 6.1 minutes. Excluding it would be inventing a schedule neither arm ran. THE THROUGHPUT RATIO, separately, is read from NON-VAL windows only (68K and 57K, reproducing the 0.838 of amendment 11) because a val-window print measures the validation pass rather than the architecture.
amendment_13:
AMENDMENT 13, 2026-09-05, written BEFORE the latent arm runs and BEFORE its code is merged. It fills in amendment 12's arm (C), the LATENT MoE, with a registered cell and -- the part a later reader needs most -- with the TWO WAYS it differs from arm (B) MoE-24, so a (C)-vs-(B) delta cannot be attributed to the projection alone.

THE REGISTERED CELL: moe_latent 384, moe_expert_ffn 2048, moe_shared_ffn 512, 24 routed + 1 shared, top-3, all 12 layers. Routed experts contract over the LATENT width: w13 (24, 4096, 384), w2 (24, 384, 2048). The token is down-projected d=1024 -> 384 ONCE PER TOKEN, the gated expert outputs are accumulated at 384, and the sum is up-projected 384 -> 1024 once; the shared expert is fed the FULL-WIDTH token and is NOT behind the projection.

PARITY IS EXACT, IN MULTIPLIES, AND MEASURED BY CONSTRUCTING THE MODULE 2026-09-05 (not arithmetic on paper): active multiplies per MoE layer = 2*d*d_latent + 3*top_k*d_latent*expert_ffn + 3*d*shared_ffn = 2*1024*384 + 3*3*384*2048 + 3*1024*512 = 786,432 + 7,077,888 + 1,572,864 = 9,437,184, identical to the dense 3*1024*3072 and to this row's own equal-active figure. The constructor asserts this EQUALITY and refuses otherwise (model.py MoEFFN.__init__), which is why the count is a refusal and not a comment.

TOTAL PARAMETERS ARE IDENTICAL TO ARM (B), NOT MERELY CLOSE: 59,006,976 per MoE layer and 800,965,704 over 12 layers, the same two integers as MoE-24 (measured by summing parameters() on both modules, 2026-09-05). The coincidence is exact and worth stating because it is what makes (C) vs (B) a clean capacity-held-fixed comparison: routed 56,623,104 in both (3*24*384*2048 = 3*24*1024*768), and the shared expert's shrink from 2,359,296 to 1,572,864 = 786,432 is EXACTLY the projection's 2*1024*384 = 786,432. So the latent arm pays for its projection out of the shared expert, at zero net parameters.

THE DIFFERENCE FROM (B) IS TWO-WAY, AND THIS IS THE CONFOUND. (C) is not '(B) plus a projection'. It differs in (i) the PROJECTION -- routed experts run at 384 instead of 1024, so the dispatch payload is 0.375x per row (384/1024) and every expert matmul contracts over 384; and (ii) the SHARED WIDTH -- 512 in (C) against 768 in (B), forced by the parity constraint once (i) is taken and the routed parameter count is held at (B)'s. A (C)-vs-(B) throughput or loss delta is therefore attributable to THE PAIR and not to the projection alone. No third arm isolating (ii) is registered this round; if (C) beats (B) on readout 1 or on wall-clock, the shared-width term stays unmeasured and the report must say so rather than crediting the projection.

WHY 384 AND NOT ANOTHER WIDTH SATISFYING PARITY. Three cells hit 1.000x exactly; 384 was taken because d_latent 384 = 3*128 divides the 128-wide head_dim evenly, so no shape in the arm is ragged against the attention layout. THE CONTROLLER'S FIRST RULING (d_latent 512, expert_ffn 1308, shared 768) DOES NOT CONSTRUCT: its active multiplies are 2*1024*512 + 3*3*512*1308 + 3*1024*768 = 9,435,136, short of dense by exactly 2,048, because 1308 came from rounding the non-integer solution 1308.444. Reported before any code was written, and the off-by-2048 config is a registered case in scripts/test_moe_latent.py so the refusal itself is tested rather than trusted.

READOUTS ARE THE ROW'S EXISTING ONES, UNCHANGED: readout 1 block-paired doc_cu val from runs/score_matrix.jsonl at equal tokens, readout 4 expert load from runs/moe_diag.jsonl with window_steps, and amendment 12's val-against-tokens AND val-against-wall-clock tables, wall-clock read from ELAPSED SECONDS per amendment_12_wall_clock and not from the tok/s prints. It CANNOT separate 'more total capacity' from 'more router choices' -- both change together when E doubles, and separating them needs a third arm at 48 experts with top_k 6 (more active compute) or 24 experts at double expert_ffn (more capacity, same choices). AMENDMENT 16, 2026-09-06, written BEFORE launch. STAGE 3: MoE-48 on the full 8B mix at world 6, on the user's 00:20Z ruling (MoE-48 is the architecture; balance, then speed, then multi-card pretrain) as relayed by 4c. Stages 1 and 2 are closed: the balancer is wired and clears its bar (outcome_amendment_15, gini@300 0.0568 against 0.3921), and the speed work is measured and landed (0041be7e, 1.265x -> 1.263x dense).

THE QUESTION: what does MoE-48 reach at 8x arm D's tokens, and does the balancer hold past 3815 steps? Amendment 15's outcome explicitly declined to claim the second -- step 300 is early in arm D's rise and the probe's own gini was still climbing (0.0337 at 200 to 0.0568 at 300) -- so this run is what answers it.

CONFIGURATION: --batch 8 --accum 4 at world 6 = 32 sequences per rank, arm D's effective batch, 192 sequences globally. mix data/mix_200m_8b.json, 786,432 tokens/step, max_steps 10173 for 8.0B tokens. --save_every 500, --val_every 200, moe_diag on, --moe_bias_gamma 0.001 (unchanged), --bf16, --no-grad_ckpt, --warmup 300, --warmdown 0.1, --anneal_frac 0, --seed 42, --moe_experts 48 --moe_top_k 3 --moe_expert_ffn 768 --moe_shared 1 --moe_layers 0-11.

THE MEMORY DECISION IS MEASURED, NOT ARITHMETIC, and it needed two points. Arm D's world-2 peak is 79.79 GiB of 80 -- 0.2 GiB of headroom -- and DDP replicates parameters, so world 6 does not reduce per-card memory at all. peak(batch) is a fixed term (parameters plus optimizer state, world-independent) plus a term linear in the per-card batch, so ONE measurement is one equation in two unknowns and any batch-8 prediction from the batch-16 point alone would be a guess. Measured at world 2 on cards 3,4, both holding 32 sequences per rank:
  batch 16 accum 2: PEAK 74.83 GiB allocated / 75.28 reserved, STARTUP 74.84 / 75.20, headroom 5.16 allocated / 4.72 RESERVED
  batch  8 accum 4: PEAK 41.65 GiB allocated / 41.89 reserved, STARTUP 41.68 / 41.89, headroom 38.32 allocated / 38.11 RESERVED
HEADROOM IS AGAINST max(PEAK, STARTUP) AND AGAINST RESERVED, and neither is a detail. STARTUP -- construction plus compile plus warmup, read before reset_peak_memory_stats -- is the larger of the two here, and it is what decides whether the shape can be LAUNCHED; PEAK decides whether each step fits once it is running. A headroom taken from PEAK alone says GO on a shape that dies during compile. And OOM is raised against RESERVED, not allocated: allocated omits the caching allocator's fragmentation, which is exactly what a 10,173-step run accumulates.
CHOSEN: b8a4, worst reserved 41.89 GiB, reserved headroom 38.11 GiB. The rule is 4c's and the reasoning is that a 7-hour job is priced by CRASH PROBABILITY, not by s/step: at 10,173 steps a single allocator fragmentation spike ends the run, and the two candidates are token-identical (same sequences per rank, same tokens per step, same step count), differing only in peak and in how many micro-batches the step splits into.

THE PROBE ITSELF WAS BROKEN UNTIL cf3148da, and this amendment records that because it means arm D's 79.79 GiB and these two numbers do not come from the same code. scripts/profile_step_cost.py never set Cfg.anneal_frac, so train.py:2286 refused to build any 200m mix (Cfg's default 0.10 against the mix's declared 0.0) -- every --peak-only invocation died in setup, before step 0. Three launches were spent on it because torchrun prints its own summary AFTER the child's traceback, so a `tail` window shows ChildFailedError and never the cause. The fix derives anneal_frac from the mix rather than adding a flag, and carries three pairwise selftest cases verified RED by mutation.

THE FIRST-100-STEP GATE, pre-registered: s/step over steps 20-100 must be at or below 2.81. That is 1.12x THIS CONFIG'S OWN measured world-2 step of 2.5094, not the b16a2 point's -- an earlier draft of this amendment pinned the gate to 2.75 from the post-fusion 2.4631, which is the OTHER candidate's number, and would have given the chosen config 1.10x where it reads as 1.12x. THE 1.12 IS A LABELLED PRIOR, NOT A MEASUREMENT: DDP's per-card ring traffic does not grow with world size, so only the latency term and the slowest-of-six tail should move, and that tail has historically been single-digit percent on this host. If the run exceeds the bar it stops and the cause is investigated rather than letting seven hours complete on an unexplained regression. Steps 0-19 are excluded because a first pass carries compile and allocator warmup (first_pass_cost_used_as_steady_state).

WHAT THE CHOICE COSTS, both sides in the same units. Both candidates push IDENTICAL tokens per step per GPU -- 131,072, i.e. 32 sequences of 4096 either way -- so the only differences are peak memory and s/step:
  b16a2  step 2.3570 s   6.66 h over 10,173 steps
  b8a4   step 2.5094 s   7.09 h over 10,173 steps
b8a4 is +6.5% per step, which over the whole run is 26 minutes, and it buys 33.39 GiB of reserved headroom. That is the trade priced explicitly rather than asserted: 26 minutes against 33 GiB, on a 7-hour job where one fragmentation spike ends the run.

THE THROUGHPUT FIGURES THE PROBE PRINTED ARE NOT USED, and the reason is a defect I found in my own instrument while reading them. The --peak-only path computed tok/s/gpu as `a.steps * B * SEQ / wall`, dropping accum, so it printed 27.8K for b16a2 and 13.0K for b8a4 -- a 2.14x gap between two configs pushing identical tokens per step, which is the accum ratio and nothing else. Reported as-is it would have read as "the b8a4 split is half the speed" and decided this very question backwards. Fixed at d0a1f935 with two selftest cases verified RED by mutation; the guarded formula 150 lines below was correct all along and the check was anchored to its name, so it never saw the second site. The numbers in this amendment are computed from step_total, which is measured by CUDA events and unaffected. PEAK and STARTUP are read from torch.cuda.max_memory_* and are also unaffected.

REGISTERED CONFOUNDS. This run is NOT a controlled pair with arm D, and reading its 1B waypoint as one would be wrong on three counts, all named here before launch so no later reader can attribute an 8B curve difference to tokens or experts when the cause is in this list:

amendment_22:
AMENDMENT 22 -- FINAL on the speed question. The two-sample arithmetic does not support
"the windows differ" either, once the confound is written down as a null. All capability and
inference claims about the +2.9% are retired; what remains on the record is two medians, two
outlier counts, and no inference. The ruling is unchanged and has been unchanged throughout:
no speed A/B, +2.9% permanently unattributed, struck on the premise.

THE TEST THAT SETTLES IT. Instead of arguing about dispersion statistics, ask directly how
often two independent 9-interval samples differ by the observed 0.0783. On this run's real
79 non-val intervals, 20000 pairs per n:
  SAME-POPULATION NULL (both windows drawn from one distribution):
    n= 9   10/20000 = 0.050%      n=19   0.000%      n=39   0.000%
  HOST-CONTENTION NULL (identical core speed, only the outlier RATE differs -- i.e. the
  projection costs nothing and the host was busier in one window), n = 9, 20000 pairs each:
     9% vs 33%   7.85% of pairs show a >= 0.0783 median gap
     9% vs 50%  32.98%
    22% vs 33%   8.79%
The two observed windows had 2 of 9 (22%) and 3 of 9 (33%) intervals in the slow band. So
under the null where the projection is free and only contention differs, the observed gap
occurs 8.79% of the time -- 176x the 0.050% false-positive rate of the same-population null.

WHY THAT ENDS IT. The only hypothesis the two-sample test excludes is that both windows came
from one population, and nobody ever proposed that. The live question was always projection
vs host, and against the host null the observed gap is unremarkable. So the arithmetic
supports "the windows differ" only against a null no one held, and supports nothing at all
about the cause. de reached the same placement independently (0.01% on a clustered
reconstruction, and the observation that the contention alternative is a different
population rather than the tested null); this session's contribution was quantifying it at
8.79%.

WHAT IS ON THE RECORD, and it carries no inference: pre-fix steps 20-100 median 2.7318 with
3 of 9 intervals in the slow band; post-fix median 2.8101 with 2 of 9; gap 0.0783 s/step
(2.9%). A 22%-vs-33% difference in contention rate alone reproduces a gap that size 8.79%
of the time. The pre-registered gate FAILED on all three statistics (median 2.8101, mean
2.8254, max 2.9018 against 2.81) and that failure stands as recorded -- a gate is a
threshold on a measurement, and the measurement was made.

THE FULL SEQUENCE OF ERRORS, all in one session, all about this session's own instrument
rather than the system under test, and every one caught by the peer rather than the author:
  1. a peer's hook duration relayed as independent confirmation with n unstated
  2. a 31-run hook median mixing a 22-run cheap population with a 6-run expensive one
  3. a "30-interval median" claimed for a 100-step arm that yields nine
  4. a two-point model chosen to prove an impossibility the data refutes (amendment 19)
  5. a bootstrap sampling WITHOUT replacement (amendment 20)
  6. max-min for sd -- a dispersion statistic unbounded in the resample count (amendment 21)
  7. a two-sample test whose null was not the confound (this amendment)
Six distinct kinds: the model, the sample size, the sampling code, the choice of statistic,
the statistic's free parameters, and the null. Evidence for the fifth: max-min on a fixed
population moves 15x across 100..16000 resamples while sd moves 0.0003 (de,
/tmp/de_stat_choice.py, seed 7).

THE RULE, in the form that would actually have caught these: not "check your instrument" --
both sessions checked, and both failed six times -- but "publish the statistic, its free
parameters, the n, and the artifact, to someone who will re-run it". Eleven instances
tonight, zero caught by the author.
amendment_23:
AMENDMENT 23 -- amendment 22's "176x" is WRONG: it divides two probabilities computed on
DIFFERENT populations. The matched-population ratio is 2.9x, not 176x. The conclusion is
unchanged -- the contention null still dominates the same-population null, so the inference
about the +2.9% is still retired and the A/B is still struck on the premise.

THE ERROR. Amendment 22 reports two figures and divides them:
  same-population null   0.050%   <- drawn from the REAL 79 intervals, whose outlier rate is 9%
  contention null        8.79%    <- 22% vs 33% outlier rates, INJECTED
  quoted ratio           176x
The two probabilities come from populations with different outlier rates, so their ratio
measures the difference in populations as much as the difference in nulls. Computed on
MATCHED populations -- both arms at 22%, the observed post-fix rate, 20000 pairs, real bands:
  same-population null   3.050%
  contention null        8.79%
  RATIO                  2.9x
Direction unchanged, magnitude overstated by 60x.

WHY IT HAPPENED, and it is the same defect twice in one amendment. This session published
"the same-population null" as 0.050% and later as 3.050% -- both correct, for different
populations, under one label. Amendment 22 then compared the earlier figure against a
contention figure built on the later population. Naming a null without naming the population
it draws from is what made the two interchangeable in the writing.

WHAT THE CORRECTED NUMBERS SUPPORT. At n = 9, on matched populations, a pure contention
difference of 22%-vs-33% produces a >= 0.0783 median gap 8.79% of the time against a 3.050%
baseline. Both are far too high to license any inference from a single observed pair, which
is amendment 22's conclusion and it does not depend on the ratio. What is NOT supported is
any statement of the form "the confound is N times more likely than chance" -- that ratio is
2.9x on matched populations and 176x as published, and the difference is entirely an artifact
of which baseline was quoted.

ALSO NOT REGISTERED, deliberately: the n-dependence of the confound. Two independent
implementations agree the confound decays with n and disagree 4x on where it stops mattering
(de: contention 0.01% at n = 39, converged with their same-population null; this session:
0.220% at n = 39 against 0.005%, a 44x ratio, not converged until n ~ 79). Because the
crossover is the exact quantity a "the A/B would have been sound at size N" claim needs, and
two implementations differ 4x on it, NO SUCH SIZE IS CLAIMED. The arithmetic does not
resurrect the A/B.

THE PATTERN, eighth instance in one session: after the model, the sample size, the sampling
code, the choice of statistic, the statistic's free parameters and the null, this one is the
BASELINE the null was compared against. The rule gains its last clause: name the statistic,
its free parameters, the n, the population the null draws from, AND the baseline any ratio is
taken against -- then hand the artifact to someone who will re-run it. Zero of tonight's
instances were caught by their own author.
amendment_24:
LAST ON THE SPEED QUESTION, and the first measurement of the zero-mean projection's cost rather than an inference about it. The projection costs 0.1470 ms per optimizer step across 12 MoE layers = 0.0052% of the run's measured 2.8228 s/step. Deleting it entirely would move s/step from 2.8228 to 2.8227. Nothing retired is revived: the +2.9% stays permanently unattributed and the speed A/B stays struck on its premise (amendments 22, 23). What this closes is the remaining question -- whether update_bias's mean subtraction is a cost worth reasoning about -- with a number instead of an argument.

THE MEASUREMENT. scripts/time_bias_projection.py on card 1 of the block, 2026-09-06 13:16:57-13:17:10Z, rc=0, 13 s. Bias tensor from the endpoint checkpoint ckpt_1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b.pt: 12 layers, 48 experts, fp32, absmax 0.209699. The script verifies its replica against MoEFFN.update_bias (38 source lines) before timing, so the timed code is the shipped code and not a paraphrase. model.py is untouched -- the no-projection arm lives inside the timing script, which is what let this run at all after the six-card A/B was struck (no off-arm exists without editing model.py on main).
  with projection      median 0.6942 ms   mean 0.6960   min 0.6581   max 0.8255   (n=1000)
  without projection   median 0.5472 ms   mean 0.5471   min 0.5174   max 0.5942   (n=1000)
  delta 0.1470 ms +/- 0.0247 (1 sd of a single step); se of the median delta 0.0010 ms
  denominator 2.8228 s/step -> 0.0052%

THE DENOMINATOR COMES FROM THE ARTIFACT, NOT FROM MEMORY, and this is load-bearing because an earlier version of this script carried two hand-written constants that were later retracted. --step-seconds has no default; the run passes --log and the script derives the figure, refusing outright if the log yields fewer than 30 steady-state step lines. It excludes warmup and val-interval lines and reads only step >= 2000. Recomputed independently from runs/1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b.log: n=769 steady-state lines, median 2.8228, mean 2.8328, min/max 2.7819/3.1192; over ALL step lines n=863, median 2.8219.

THE RULING'S OWN DENOMINATOR IS STALE, recorded here so the next reader does not hunt for it. card_assignment.json's lane_to (fb 2026-09-06T07:4xZ) says "report ms/step for 12 layers beside the 2.8121 s/step". 2.8121 is not any statistic of this run: not the steady-state median, not the mean, not the all-lines median. It was written at 07:4xZ while the run was still going and most likely comes from the 02:4xZ grant's gate figure ("2.81 s/step over steps 20-100"). It changes nothing here -- both denominators give 0.0052% to four places, because the delta is four orders of magnitude smaller than either -- but a number on the record has to be one that can be recomputed from an artifact.

INTERLEAVING IS THE CONFOUND CONTROL; THE ARM-INTERNAL SPREAD IS NOT. The arms are sampled interleaved (one 'with' then one 'without', 1000 times), not arm-after-arm, and the arm order is fixed because rows[0] - rows[1] is the reported delta. The selftest measures what the discarded design would have done, on a simulated true delta of 0.0800 ms:
     drift(ms)   arm-after-arm   interleaved
          0.00          0.0813        0.0799
          0.05          0.0533        0.0807
          0.20         -0.0183        0.0835
At 0.20 ms of drift the sequential estimate CHANGES SIGN and the script prints "this timer cannot resolve the projection's cost" -- word for word what it prints on a genuine null. Under the sequential design "cannot resolve" and "does not exist" are the same output, which is why the design was changed rather than the threshold. Interleaving charges drift to within-arm noise instead of to the between-arm difference.

Separately reported and NOT a significance claim: the p95 of |x - median| on the 'with' arm is 0.0359 ms, below the delta. That says within-arm spread is smaller than the difference; it says nothing about a systematic between-arm offset, because a within-arm dispersion statistic is blind to one. The confound control is the interleaving, not this number.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEASURE: wall-clock cost inside a real training step (the timing is the update_bias call in isolation, one card, no DDP, no optimizer, no router forward), and any effect of the projection on convergence. The first is deliberate -- the question ruled 2026-09-06T08:1xZ was the projection's own cost with no host confound. The second is the balance question, answered by the gini series and b0-28, not here.

EVIDENCE: scripts/time_bias_projection.py selftest PASS, 9 checks (the guard fires on a replica whose projection is deleted and on one where it is not last, passes the shipped form; p95 stable while half-range grows with n; the denominator excludes warmup and val lines and refuses a short log; interleaving cancels a drift that flips arm-after-arm's sign). Log /tmp/b0_step2.log on the pod. Grant: card_assignment.json lane_to step (2), fb 2026-09-06T07:4xZ as amended 08:1xZ.
amendment_25:
CORRECTS AMENDMENT 24's claim that the ruling's 2.8121 s/step "is not any statistic of this run". It IS one: 2.8121 is the median of the run's PRE-2000 steady rows -- step 20-1990 with 200/500 multiples and the first step dropped -- to six places (2.812100, n=94). Amendment 24 called it stale and guessed it came from the 02:4xZ grant's gate window ("2.81 s/step over steps 20-100"); both halves are withdrawn. The projection conclusion is unchanged: 0.1470 ms against 2.8121 and against 2.8228 both give 0.0052%, because the delta is four orders of magnitude below either denominator.

HOW THE ERROR WAS MADE, because the shape matters more than the number. Amendment 24 checked three candidate statistics -- the steady-state median (2.8228), the mean (2.8328), the all-lines median (2.8219) -- found 2.8121 among none of them, and concluded it was not any statistic of the run. Three candidates is not an exhaustive search. The window that produces it is the one the amendment itself never computed: everything BELOW its own lower bound. Checking the guessed attribution too: steps 20-100 yields n=0 rows under the rule, so that provenance was wrong as well. fb wrote the ruling at 07:4xZ with the run near step 5000, and a median taken then is weighted toward the warmup rows -- a correct number from a different window, which amendment 24 read as an expired one.

WHAT THE >=2000 BOUND ACTUALLY CUTS, measured on both arms after e1 (lessons-58) proposed the test. It does not separate two distributions:
  MoE   1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b   step 20-1990  n=94   median 2.8121   |  step >=2000  n=769  median 2.8228   (+0.38%)
  dense 0.2b_8b_b192        step 20-1990  n=187  median 2.8121-equivalent 2.1541  |  step >=2000  n=36  median 2.1543   (+0.01%)
The premise behind the bound -- that the warmup lr ramp inflates s/step -- was never verified by either of us and does not hold on either arm. lr affects loss, not step time. The bound is still worth keeping, because it excludes the compile-warmed first step (5.2438 on this arm, the max of the pre-2000 window) without needing a separate first-step rule, but it should be described as what it is: a cheap way to drop startup cost, not a boundary between two regimes.

THE EXTRACTION RULE CHANGED ONE PREDICATE since amendment 24, and 2.8228 is unaffected. Amendment 24's rule dropped rows carrying "this interval". That marker is a RELATIVE threshold, not an IO label: train.py:176-182 emits it when `over > 0.2 * win_mean`. On this arm every contaminated row clears 20% (save steps +59.2%, median 4.4942 against 2.8228; val steps +35.5%), so coverage was 49 of 49 and the filter looked exact. It is not exact -- it is threshold-dependent. On the dense comparator the same contamination raises s/step only 17%, falls under the threshold, and 3 rows leak. The rule now drops rows by step number (step % 200 == 0 or step % 500 == 0), which on THIS arm selects a byte-identical set (49 marked rows == 49 multiples, 0 marked non-multiples, sorted(a) == sorted(b) is True), so the published 2.8228 stands unchanged while the dense arm is filtered correctly.

Evidence: recomputed on the pod from runs/1.5b-a0.2b-e48_8b.log, 2026-09-06. Prior art for the error class in this same prereg: amendments 19-20 (max-min as a statistic), 22-23 (a ratio across two populations). This one is narrower and the same family -- a claim of exhaustion after a partial search.

question: At 200M dense parameters, how many EXPOSURES n of a constructed-absent skill does pretraining need before test accuracy leaves the floor? The number nobody has is accuracy vs n on S_test; the deliverable is the shape of that curve, including the case where it never leaves the floor, which is a bound and still an answer.
context: Continued pretraining of ckpt_b0_headmix_armA.pt (206,128,200 dense params, d1024 L12 h8 ffn3072 attn_every=4, 1B tokens on mix_200m_8b, seed 42, world 2, 3815 steps) on its own mix with S documents injected. S/P are 3b's constructed-absent operator sets frozen at 0389a5ef (facts/contamination.json#cont.novel_ops_frozen_sets): a @ b = 3a - 2b + 1 evaluated right to left, with a carry that adds 10 EXACTLY once when an intermediate is negative. The operator, its rule and its phrasing were invented 2026-09-05, after every corpus in the mix was built -- so absence is CONSTRUCTED, not certified by a scan (cont.novel_operator_collision bounds rule-phrasing collision below 0.0029% in 105,000 docs, not at zero).

arms.n1: 1 exposure of the fixed 1,000-document S set. 104,000 injected tokens, 0.079% of the arm.
arms.control_arm: NO S injection, P injected identically, same 500 steps and same total tokens. This is the floor the curve is read against -- NOT ckpt_b0_headmix_armA itself, because 500 more steps of its own mix moves its non-S metrics on their own.

ladder_and_its_bound: n in {1, 8, 64, 256} (4c's ruling on e1's measurement). n=512 and n=4096 were in the original design and are NOT run: at 104.0 tokens/doc mean, 4096 exposures is 425,984,000 injected tokens = 325% of a 500-step arm's 131,072,000, so the arm would be fine-tuning on S with pretraining mixed in rather than continued pretraining with an injection. n > 256 is reported as a BOUND ('no movement through 256 exposures'), never as a measured zero.
exposure_definition: n = EPOCHS over one fixed 1,000-document set (reading B). The alternative reading -- n DISTINCT documents seen once each -- is a different experiment about breadth rather than repetition, is NOT run here, and is cheap if wanted (4096 distinct docs = 425,984 tokens = 1.6 steps). Named so the two are never conflated in a later reading.
readout_1_primary: 4-way LIKELIHOOD on S_test_4way: score each option, take the argmax, compare to `label`. SUPERSEDED IN THIS ROW'S FIRST VERSION, which said 'three distractors that are the answers under the three competing readings of the carry rule', floor 0.25, MDE 0.3060. All three are wrong now: the set uses an 8-rung misreading ladder because a three-reading version leaves only 457/1000 items with four distinct values; the floor is not 0.25 (see readout_1_instrument); and the MDE follows the floor. READ readout_1_instrument FOR THE OPERATIVE SPECIFICATION -- sha, prior lower bound, control-arm operational floor, per-program MDE. This key states only the readout's form and the reason its distractors carry its power. The distractor construction is 3b's, reviewed by e1; it is the readout's whole power, because add-once and add-until differ on 41.8% of diamond_chain and 56.2% of diamond_chain4 (e1's recount of 3b's per-program measurement) and on 0% of P.
readout_1_why_not_exact_match: Exact-match CANNOT move on this control and was the original specification. Measured: the control's generation accuracy is l1_fewshot acc 0.0322 (16/497, answer_present_rate 0.670) on grade-school word problems it TRAINED on. S needs three-to-four-step composition plus a conditional carry in an invented notation, so its expected exact-match is 0, and 0/1000 correct gives a 95% upper bound of 0.0030. MDE from a zero floor is 0.0078 -- 8 correct items out of 1000. The curve would have two reachable states, 0 and 8-items, and 'every arm reads 0' would be indistinguishable from 'the readout has no power'. NOT a counterexample: math_v2_like 0.9628 on this same checkpoint is a 2-way LIKELIHOOD score with a 50% floor (eval/math_v2_like.py docstring), not generation.
readout_2_secondary: S_test exact-match, same items, greedy. Reported at every n. A lift here is a strictly stronger result than readout 1 and would be reported as such.
readout_1_2_joint_reading: A likelihood lift with exact-match still at 0 means RULE PREFERRED, NOT YET EXECUTABLE: the model ranks the add-once answer above the two wrong readings but cannot produce it. That is a real, reportable state of the curve and the most likely outcome at 200M -- it is the readout's designed middle, not a failed measurement.
readout_3_format_floor_and_stop: P_test, same 4-way likelihood, in every arm. P is the FORMAT control: same glyph, same rule sentence, one application, no composition, and its carry NEVER fires (e1 measured 0 of 5,096 items; all three readings agree on every P item by construction). So P movement is format acquisition, not skill. STOP RULE: if P moves by more than its own MDE while S does not, the arm learned the notation and the S reading is void for that n.
confound_dilution: At n=256 the injection is 20.312% of the arm's tokens, so that arm sees 79.7% as much natural mix as the control arm. Any non-S difference at n=256 confounds skill acquisition with mix dilution. Read, not waved: the control arm's non-S metrics (domain_bpb, lambada_en/zh, humaneval_bpb) are scored at the same step and the n=256 arm's are compared against them; a dilution effect there is reported alongside the S number. n=1, 8 and 64 are 0.079%/0.635%/5.078% and are not materially diluted.
confound_document_leak: ~39 S documents share each 4,097-token row (train.py:1899-1903 reshapes the eos-separated stream). Cfg.doc_mask=True resets KDA state and SWA per <eos>, but Cfg.conv_doc_isolated is False in the control and the arms MUST match it -- passing --conv_doc_isolated would change the topology relative to the checkpoint being continued (eff.kda_document_isolation_violated, 48.88 at the block-0 output against a 0.9253 tolerance). So the short_conv leak across document boundaries is PRESENT, identically in every arm and in the control arm. It is a shared condition, not a between-arm confound, and it means every n has ~39 S documents in mutual context -- which if anything helps the arms and cannot manufacture a false floor.
injection_recipe: datagen/build_s_inject.py writes data/corpus/s_inject_n<N>/s_inject_000.jsonl holding the 1,000 S documents repeated N times, and data/corpus/p_format/ holding the 1,000 P documents ONCE (P's exposure count must not vary with n, or a P movement could not be read). Documents are instruction + worked solution lines + answer: the skill is the PROCEDURE and the solution lines are where the procedure is; injecting question->answer alone would teach 1,000 answers, and S_test shares no instance with S_pool, so the curve would read zero at every n for a reason unrelated to exposures. Repeats are INTERLEAVED by a seeded permutation (20260905 + n) over the whole N*1,000 list, not written as N contiguous blocks -- contiguous blocks put every exposure of a document inside a few hundred adjacent steps, which measures massed repetition rather than exposures distributed over training. The builder refuses a pool whose sha256 is not the frozen one and refuses to overwrite an existing shard directory, both mutation-verified.
how_the_documents_enter_the_schedule: As an ordinary corpus shard read through a mix domain, NOT a code path. train.py tokenizes data/corpus/<domain>/*.jsonl, caches to tokens_<domain>.pt, and build_mix allocates rows per domain, shuffles within each phase (train.py:2195, torch.randperm under generator g seeded by sample_seed) and stripes by rank (:2241, mine = plan[:, :n][:, rank::world]). A build_mix hook would be a second scheduling path used by one experiment, bypassing the shuffle and stripe this experiment's exposure schedule depends on. Each arm gets its own mix file with s_inject_n<N> and p_format added at epochs 1 and the other nine domains rescaled by (1 - w_S) -- so the arm's non-S composition is the control's, proportionally.
world_size_and_why: WORLD 2, matching the control. Not world 1 even though one arm per card would be faster: the plan is rank-striped at train.py:2241, so world 1 changes WHICH documents each rank sees and therefore changes the exposure schedule itself -- the quantity under measurement. Cards 5 and 7 sequentially, 500 steps per arm, 5 arms = 0.66B tokens total, 1.1 GPU-pair hours (~2.2 card-hours) at the control's 82,300 tok/s/gpu.
token_accounting: This experiment reports CONSUMED tokens and generated = 0; 3b's RLVR recipe reports GENERATED and consumed = 0. Both ledgers carry both column names with the other at zero (4c's ruling). A single 'tokens' column would silently add two different quantities -- an exposure the model reads and a rollout the model writes -- and the pretraining-vs-RL comparison this pairs with is exactly a comparison of those two.

decision_each_readout_changes.readout_1_clears_MDE_at_some_n: That n is the conversion point at 200M, and it becomes the pretraining-side number the RLVR comparison is read against. Decides whether the RL comparison is run at all: if pretraining needs 256 exposures for a 4-way lift, an RL run generating far fewer trajectories cannot be expected to beat it and the comparison's budget has to be matched to this.
decision_each_readout_changes.readout_1_flat_through_256: The answer is a BOUND: 200M does not convert this skill within 256 exposures at 0.66B continued-pretraining tokens. Decides that the conversion question moves to a larger model or a longer budget rather than to more exposures, and kills the equal-exposure form of the RL comparison at this scale.
decision_each_readout_changes.readout_2_moves: Rule executable, not merely preferred. Strictly stronger and would be reported as the headline.
decision_each_readout_changes.readout_3_P_moves_while_S_does_not: That arm measured format acquisition. Void for that n; the recipe needs P's exposure count reduced or its items changed before that n is re-read.
decision_each_readout_changes.dilution_shows_at_n256: n=256 is reported with its non-S deltas attached and the ladder's top point is treated as confounded rather than clean.

amendment_1: CSA as merged at 8c2308b7 is NOT DeepSeek-V4's CSA, and a null result here must be read as this operator rather than as the reference (3b review of PR #78, measured against facts/deepseek_v4.json#dsv4.hybrid_attention rather than the PR's prose). Two divergences. (1) GROUPING IS NON-OVERLAPPING: kp.view(B,H,nb,m,D) pools exactly [b*m, b*m+m), where the reference specifies 'overlapped grouping draws from 2m=8 neighbors'. Enumerated at T=12 m=4, the implementation gives [0-3][4-7][8-11] and the reference would give [0-3][0-7][4-11]; at the default csa_compress=16 the block-boundary effect is 4x coarser than the reference's m=4. (2) NO LIGHTNING INDEXER: selection is idx = sc.topk(...) over the same q.kc the coarse branch computed, where the reference uses a separate low-dim indexer (64 heads, dim 128) so selection is not tied to the coarse attention's own scoring -- the select branch therefore cannot disagree with the compress branch about where to look. Both are defensible simplifications for a reference implementation and the docstring correctly cites the NSA/DSA family (arXiv 2502.11089), not DSv4. THE SMOKE-TEST EXPECTATION, so the first odd steps are not diagnosed as a bug: the branch gate is three INDEPENDENT sigmoids, not a convex mixture, so at zero-init every branch contributes 0.5 and the three sum -- measured dense out RMS 0.0441 vs CSA 0.0533, 1.21x into the residual stream at step 0. 'None is born dominant' holds for the relative weights and not for the sum. Parity itself is confirmed: flag off is torch.equal to origin/main's GatedMLA (15,360 params, identical key sets, max|delta| 0.0) and flag on differs at 0.154; causality is clean at all 16 positions for BOTH k and v, the v channel being a second leak path a score-only test cannot fail on.
